source_row.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories lists the adult potassium reference interval as 3.6 to 5.2 mmol/L and notes that low extracellular potassium can produce muscle weakness; values below 3.0 mmol/L are associated with marked neuromuscular symptoms. A value of 2.9 mEq/L is therefore hypokalemia, making Option C correct. The other options either identify a different electrolyte abnormality or incorrectly classify the measured potassium as normal.
source_row.source_detail: Mayo Clinic Laboratories Test KS/602352, Potassium, Serum — Reference Values: age >=1 year 3.6-5.2 mmol/L. Clinical Information/Interpretation: decreased extracellular potassium is characterized by muscle weakness and cardiac conduction abnormalities; potassium below 3.0 mmol/L is associated with marked neuromuscular symptoms. source_row.stem: An adult client has a serum potassium level of 2.9 mEq/L and reports new muscle weakness. Which interpretation is most accurate?
